subject.title: [Bug]: Agents should not be able to access or modify files outside their own working space.

question: Should OpenClaw make per-agent workspaces a hard default filesystem boundary, keep the current compatibility default with opt-in `tools.fs.workspaceOnly` and sandboxing, or route this entirely to a broader path-policy design?
rationale: The remaining work changes a security boundary and a documented default that existing users may rely on, and the current open PRs demonstrate competing scopes for file tools versus shell execution.

options.title: Make workspace confinement the default
options.body: Define a secure default, migration story, and explicit exec treatment before merging the implementation that enforces it.

options.title: Keep opt-in compatibility defaults
options.body: Leave current behavior in place but improve setup, doctor warnings, and docs so operators deliberately choose workspace-only or sandboxed agents.

options.title: Route to the path-policy tracker
options.body: Make the configurable filesystem policy issue the canonical implementation path and keep this issue linked until the concrete user report is covered.

recommendation.title: Make workspace confinement the default
recommendation.body: Define a secure default, migration story, and explicit exec treatment before merging the implementation that enforces it.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history on the workspace-only guard and current filesystem policy resolver, and prior reviews framed this as a maintainer security/default decision.
